title: Keep a QA claim from superseding the worker's finalizing attempt before its landing is acknowledged
description:
DEFECT reported 2026-09-14 by qa-f0f9ea9e while reviewing task-49ec8755, reproduced in a scratch fixture. Evidence: the task-49ec8755 rejection comment and #general msg-1a7d6192.

WHAT HAPPENS
1. complete_task moves the task to REVIEW and parks the worker's attempt in `finalizing`. The wrapper is expected to record the candidate and call finalize_attempt after the CLI exits.
2. A QA seat claims the REVIEW row. In claimNextTask.ts, openClaimAttempt hits ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN and calls closeOpenAttempts. That closes every open phase, including `finalizing`, and opens a new generation for QA.
3. The worker wrapper's post-flight then calls record_candidate with its pinned identity. record_candidate is fenced to the current attempt, so it refuses with ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED. docs/MCP_SERVER.md says the runner records after complete_task "when QA may already own the REVIEW task", so this contradicts the documented contract.
4. task-49ec8755's wrappers record a candidate before every completion landing, even when no qualityGate is configured. The refusal therefore turns the landing into MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, a rescue ref, and a stopped worker loop.
5. The qa_approve finalizing hold never fires either, because the claim already closed the attempt.

LIVE EVIDENCE
- task-9e851: QA generation 2 closed worker generation 1 about 40s after TASK_COMPLETED (2026-09-13 18:43:10Z).
- task-49ec8755: qa-f0f9ea9e's claim closed attempt-bc658bb5 (generation 1, finalizing) at 2026-09-14 18:29Z.

EXPOSURE. Every seat launched from the repo launcher now runs task-49ec8755's wrapper code, committed as checkpoint 65b2702. Any completion that loses this race stops its worker seat. The bytes survive in a rescue ref and are recovered by the claiming seat's pre-flight.

DECISION NEEDED (architect chooses)
A. Daemon: a claim by a different worker must not close another worker's finalizing attempt before finalize_attempt. Either refuse the claim with a retryable ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, or keep the finalizing record addressable by record_candidate and finalize_attempt after the supersede.
B. Wrapper: record a candidate only when a gate will actually run, and treat ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED at landing as "QA already owns the row", not as a gate failure.
C. Both, for defence in depth.

CONSTRAINTS
- Keep the finalizing hold's purpose: neither the worker's next claim nor qa_approve may race past an unacknowledged landing.
- No timeouts based on lastActivityAt or any other idle signal.
- Coordinate with task-2a7e0f5b, which is editing claimNextTask.ts and attemptStore.ts right now. That overlap is why this card depends on it.
- Any wrapper-side change must touch both launchers, keep parity, and be coordinated with task-49ec8755's rework.
definitionOfDone: A QA claim of a REVIEW row whose worker attempt is still finalizing no longer breaks that worker's completion landing: the completion commit lands, with no rescue ref and no stopped loop

Tests cover complete_task, then a QA claim, then record_candidate and finalize_attempt from the worker's pinned identity, and enforce the chosen rule (claim refusal, or a superseded finalizing attempt that stays acknowledgeable)
qa_approve cannot approve a row whose worker landing has been neither acknowledged nor superseded under the chosen rule, and a test proves it

docs/MCP_SERVER.md states the rule for claim_next_task, record_candidate and finalize_attempt; npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass in packages/moe-daemon, and both postflight harnesses and parity checks pass if the launchers change
taskRails: Never gate, close or release an attempt based on lastActivityAt or any other idle signal
If the launchers change, change scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 together and keep parity-check green

implementationPlan.description: Phase 1+2 — Confirm the chain at HEAD before editing; no code changes in this step. Post ONE task comment with the findings and the design decision. task-2a7e0f5b is DONE and landed (90277ac); every line below is at HEAD. (a) The race: completeTask.ts parks the attempt in `finalizing` (~149-152) BEFORE its WORKING→REVIEW write clears the seat (~156-173). A QA claim of the unassigned REVIEW row passes the worker-scoped finalizing hold in claimNextTask.ts (~271-282, `a.workerId === params.workerId`), writes the assignment (~463), and openClaimAttempt (~48-72) hits ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN (finalizing is in OPEN_PHASES, attemptStore.ts ~56); arm 3 calls `closeOpenAttempts(state, taskId)` (~70), closing the worker's finalizing attempt and opening a QA generation. Both holds are then gone: qaApprove.ts ~79 finds no finalizing attempt, and the worker's next claim is no longer refused. (b) The wrapper fails before the RPC: moe_attempt_read (moe-agent.sh ~1875-1892) and Read-MoeAttempt (moe-agent.ps1 ~1275-1288) require exactly one open attempt owned by the worker, so after the supersede they fail with `identity`, and the completion becomes MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE plus a rescue ref plus a stopped loop. Once no other seat can close the finalizing attempt, the worker's attempt stays the only open one and that pre-check passes — which is how this daemon-only change satisfies DoD 1. Both wrappers claim through the ranked pool only (CLAIM_JSON carries no taskId), so the explicit-path refusal never reaches a wrapper. The wrapper-side hardening belongs to task-49ec8755's rework per the governor. (c) Nothing else ends a finalizing attempt on an unassigned REVIEW row: releaseWorkerTasks (workerLifecycle.ts ~128), deleteWorker (workerStore.ts ~261), purgeAllWorkers (~416) and release_task's unassigned branch (releaseTask.ts ~199-233) all select by assignment; closeHandedBackAttempts spares finalizing (attemptStore.ts ~483-487); reconcileRunningAttempts (~372) and runReconcileWindowSweep (sweeps.ts ~218) skip it; reattach refuses it. So refusing third-party claims without a close path would wedge a row whose wrapper exits without finalizing. (d) Wake gap: attemptStore emits no event (header ~22-26); wait_for_task's subscriber reacts only to TASK_CREATED/TASK_UPDATED (waitForTask.ts ~383). `state.emit` is annotated @internal for state/* modules (StateManager.ts ~978-979) and no tool calls it, so the wake belongs in a state-side helper. The emitter is wsServer.broadcast (index.ts ~597, re-serving the task through deliveryProjection); the subscribers are waitForTask (~356), waitForResource (~143, RESOURCE_UPDATED only) and chatWait (~91, MESSAGE_CREATED/CHANNEL_DELETED only) — an extra TASK_UPDATED with an unchanged task only re-runs wait_for_task's matcher and clears the board's finalizing badge. (e) finalize_attempt has no worker gate and OUTCOMES = landed | nothing-to-commit | rescued | failed, so a governor or human can close an abandoned boundary with `outcome: 'failed'`. (f) Tests that pass today only because arm 3 closes another worker's finalizing attempt — FIVE insert points in four tests: src/__e2e__/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts 'runs a clean lifecycle…' (QA claim ~150), 'drives a rejection cycle…' (QA claims ~184 AND ~205, after two complete_task calls at generations 1 and 3), 'auto-flips to PLANNING when the same DoD item fails twice' (~234; its second REVIEW entry ~246 is a direct updateTask with no attempt), and src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts '…across a full lifecycle' (~317). claimNextTask.test.ts ~1239 and ~1262 claim a DIFFERENT task and stay green. finalizeAttempt.test.ts ~115-126 pins the PERSISTED attempt record's key set; this plan persists no new field. DESIGN DECISION (record it): option A, refuse — no seat other than the attempt's own worker may claim a task whose attempt is finalizing; the explicit-taskId path refuses with a retryable ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, the ranked pool and the wait_for_task matcher skip the row, a real finalize wakes waiters, and deregister_worker closes its own worker's finalizing attempts so an exiting runner cannot wedge the row. Rejected: keeping the finalizing record acknowledgeable beside a new QA attempt (breaks assertNoOpenAttempt, currentAttempt, the equality fence in assertAttemptCurrent, and both wrappers' exactly-one-open readers); a persisted supersede marker (schema addition); wrapper-only option B (cannot restore the qa_approve hold, and a gated landing still needs a candidate the fence refuses). The refusal stays limited to phase `finalizing` held by a different worker: task-2a7e0f5b relies on arm 3 to close running/reconciling leftovers on unassigned rows.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 3 — Tests first, in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptHandback.test.ts. Existing helpers: seedClaimedWorkingRow (creates only task-W, then loads — create any other row BEFORE calling it), DONE_PLAN, claim (always sends taskId), claimForReview (claim + get_context), phases, refusal; afterEach already clears the emitter. Add imports recordCandidateTool '../tools/recordCandidate.js', finalizeAttemptTool '../tools/finalizeAttempt.js', qaApproveTool '../tools/qaApprove.js', qaRejectTool '../tools/qaReject.js', waitForTaskTool and activeWaiters '../tools/waitForTask.js', deregisterWorkerTool '../tools/deregisterWorker.js'; clear activeWaiters in afterEach. New describe 'a finalizing landing is not superseded by another seat'. Assert exact codeName, code -32002, context and `[generation, phase]` tuples — never a bare truthy check. Cases (RED = fails on HEAD; GUARD = green before and after): (1) RED race, DoD 1-3: seedClaimedWorkingRow({ implementationPlan: DONE_PLAN }) for worker-1 → complete_task { taskId, workerId: 'worker-1', verification: { command: 'npm test', exitCode: 0 } } → phases [[1,'finalizing']], row REVIEW and unassigned. QA explicit claim { statuses: ['REVIEW'], taskId, workerId: 'qa-1' } → throws ATTEMPT_FINALIZING with context { attemptId, generation: 1, taskId, workerId: 'worker-1', retryable: true } and a message naming worker-1, the attempt id and moe.finalize_attempt; afterwards the row is still unassigned, qa-1 holds no attempt, phases still [[1,'finalizing']]. record_candidate with worker-1's pinned identity (attemptId/generation from the complete_task response, id 'cand-1', baseRevision 'a1'×20, treeSha 'c3'×20, deliveryTarget 'refs/heads/wave1-pilot') succeeds. qa_approve { taskId, workerId: 'qa-1', summary } is refused ATTEMPT_FINALIZING (the hold runs before the ownership checks, so this proves DoD 3 in this sequence). finalize_attempt { taskId, attemptId, generation: 1, workerId: 'worker-1', runnerId: 'worker-1', outcome: 'landed', landedRevision: 'b2'×20 } → [[1,'closed']]. The QA claim retried returns generation 2; get_context stamps qa-1; qa_approve { …, candidateId: 'cand-1' } succeeds. (2) RED ranked pool: while finalizing, `call(claimNextTaskTool(h.state), { statuses: ['REVIEW'], workerId: 'qa-1' })` (not the claim helper) returns hasNext false and opens no attempt — it must skip, never throw; after finalize it returns the row at generation 2. (3) RED wake: first await a waiter { statuses: ['REVIEW'], workerId: 'qa-1', timeoutMs: 1000 } to its `timedOut: true` result while finalizing (waiters are keyed by workerId, so never overlap two). Then start a second waiter with timeoutMs 5000, sleep ~50 ms, assert `activeWaiters.has('qa-1')` (proves it parked and did not match immediately), call finalize_attempt, await it and assert hasNext true and task.id — no wall-clock assertion. (4) RED deregister close: complete_task, then deregister_worker for worker-1 without a finalize → phases [[1,'closed']], a QA claim then succeeds at generation 2. Variant A: after complete_task delete worker-1's record first (h.state.deleteWorker or the prune path), then deregister_worker → the attempt still closes (keyed on attempt.workerId). Variant B: a DEAD worker-1 that still holds a finalizing attempt → deregister_worker closes it and returns alreadyDead true, and no new #workers/#governors chat line or WORKER_DISCONNECTED activity row is written. (5) GUARD own hold unchanged: create task-2 WORKING order 2 BEFORE seedClaimedWorkingRow; after complete_task, worker-1's claim of task-2 is still refused with the existing worker-scoped message. (6) GUARD escape: finalize_attempt { taskId, attemptId, generation: 1, workerId: 'governor-1', runnerId: 'governor-1', outcome: 'failed' } closes it and a QA claim then succeeds. (7) GUARD reject bypass: complete_task → qa_reject { taskId, reason } with no workerId (the human path) → row WORKING, phases still [[1,'finalizing']] → worker-2's explicit claim { statuses: ['WORKING'], taskId, workerId: 'worker-2' } is refused ATTEMPT_FINALIZING → after finalize_attempt it succeeds at generation 2. (8) GUARD arm-3 orphan cleanup from task-2a7e0f5b: the existing unassigned-row running/reconciling cases in this file stay green untouched. Error handling in the tests: every waiter is awaited before the case ends, so no timer leaks into the next case.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 4a — packages/moe-daemon/src/util/claimEligibility.ts: the shared rule, so claim_next_task and wait_for_task stay in lockstep (the rule stated at the top of that module and at claimNextTask.ts ~350-355). Add: (1) `finalizingAttemptsByTask(state: StateManager): Map<string, ExecutionAttempt>` — one pass over listAttempts(state) keeping each task's attempt in phase `finalizing`; build it once per claim or match call, never per candidate (listAttempts copies and sorts, so a per-row call is O(tasks × attempts)). (2) `foreignFinalizingAttempt(index, taskId, workerId: string | undefined): ExecutionAttempt | null` — the task's finalizing attempt when its workerId differs from the caller; a caller without a workerId counts as foreign (claim_next_task without a workerId assigns nothing and opens no attempt, so this only turns a read-only peek into a skip or refusal). (3) `foreignFinalizingRefusal(attempt: ExecutionAttempt): MoeError` — STATE_CONFLICT with codeName ATTEMPT_FINALIZING (import the exported constant from util/claimGuards.ts; do not edit that file), context { attemptId, generation, taskId, workerId: attempt.workerId, retryable: true }, and a message written for the refused seat, not for the runner: `Task <taskId> is held by worker <workerId>'s attempt <attemptId> (generation <g>) in phase finalizing: its bytes are not landed yet, so no other seat may claim it. This is a RETRYABLE refusal (context.retryable) — retry after that worker's runner calls moe.finalize_attempt. If worker <workerId> is gone for good, a governor or human closes the boundary with moe.finalize_attempt { taskId, attemptId, generation, outcome: 'failed' }.` (The existing attemptFinalizingRefusal tells its reader to finalize, which is the wrong advice for a QA caller.) Error handling: the index skips any record that is not a well-formed attempt instead of throwing, so one bad record cannot take every claim down.

util/claimEligibility.ts (+107/-1, LF kept):
- finalizingAttemptsByTask(state): one pass over listAttempts that keeps each task's finalizing attempt. Records come in generation order, so the highest one wins.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 4b — packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts. The real guards are (1) and (2); (3) is defence in depth. (1) Explicit-taskId path: right after the needsHumanReview refusal (~306-311) and before ownedBySelf, the dependsOn gate and the claimable/replaceExisting check (~313-330), build the index and `throw foreignFinalizingRefusal(held)` when `foreignFinalizingAttempt(index, requested.id, params.workerId)` returns one — before any eviction or assignment write, so a refused claim writes nothing. The attempt's own worker never reaches it (the worker-scoped hold ~271 refuses that worker first). (2) Ranked pool (~343-356): add `.filter((t) => !foreignFinalizingAttempt(index, t.id, params.workerId))` beside `isClaimGatedByDependsOn`; it skips silently, because a thrown refusal on the ranked path reads as a dead daemon to the sh wrapper (moe_rpc exits 1 and the pre-flight logs 'claim_next_task stopped answering'). With (1) and (2) in place, the eviction closes at ~413 (inactive owner) and ~429 (replaceExisting), which call closeOpenAttempts and would close a finalizing attempt, can no longer see another worker's finalizing row. (3) Backstop in openClaimAttempt arm 3 only: when the ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN leftover is phase `finalizing` and owned by another worker, throw foreignFinalizingRefusal instead of closing it. No tool path reaches it today (the board cannot set assignedWorkerId — WebSocketServer.ts UPDATE_TASK denylist), so no claim_next_task test is required; for a non-resume claim the existing handBackUnrecordedClaim undoes the assignment write, and its null write closes only running/reconciling, never the finalizing attempt. Arm 3 keeps closing running and reconciling leftovers exactly as today. (4) Comments: rewrite the worker-scoped hold comment (~268-270, 'another worker's finalizing attempt is none of this caller's business') to point at the task-scoped third-party hold now in the claim path, and rewrite the arm-3 doc (~36-47) so it no longer implies a finalizing attempt can be superseded. Error handling: the index build cannot throw (step 4a); no write happens before either refusal. Make step 2's cases (1), (2), (5) and (7) green.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 4c — Wait and wake. packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts: add one state-side helper, `announceAttemptClosed(state: StateManager, taskId: string): void`, that emits `{ type: 'TASK_UPDATED', payload: task }` for the task when it still exists (no activity row, no updatedAt change), and update the store header (~22-26, 'appends no activity row and emits no event') to name this single, deliberate exception: the one event that lets wait_for_task waiters and the board see that a finalizing boundary ended. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/finalizeAttempt.ts: after the single close write (~224), when the attempt really moved from finalizing to closed, call announceAttemptClosed; the idempotent closed replay (~200) calls nothing. The tool never calls the @internal state.emit directly. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/waitForTask.ts: in findMatchingTask's eligible chain (~158-168) add the same `foreignFinalizingAttempt` filter with one index per call, so a row claim_next_task would skip is never wait-visible (otherwise QA seats spin wake → claim → nothing); it stays inside the eligible chain so the solo NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP routing (~201) is unaffected. Error handling: the emit runs after the durable write (setAttemptPhase publishes the closed record before returning), and state.emit already isolates subscriber errors, so a subscriber can never observe the attempt still open or fail the tool. Make step 2's cases (2) and (3) green.

Phase 4d — Close path for an exiting runner. packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerLifecycle.ts deregisterWorker (~174-192). (1) FIRST, before the missing-record early return (~179-182), close every attempt with `attempt.workerId === workerId && phase === 'finalizing'` through setAttemptPhase(…, 'closed'), each in its own try/catch (log { workerId, attemptId, taskId, error } and continue), then announceAttemptClosed for each affected task. Keyed on the attempt, it still works when the worker record was already pruned (a post-flight gate longer than staleWorkerTimeoutMs lets the Layer-3 sweep delete the record while the attempt is finalizing). (2) Close-only retry: when the worker record is DEAD with no assigned task (the existing alreadyDead short-circuit ~188), keep returning alreadyDead true WITHOUT re-posting chat, activity or WORKER_DELETED — the close in (1) has already run, so a retry after a failed close closes again quietly and the documented idempotency holds. The return shape and tools/deregisterWorker.ts stay unchanged. (3) Comment the rationale precisely: deregister_worker is sent only from exit and teardown paths — after the landing, its rescue, or its abandonment — so it never cuts a live landing short; it is NOT evidence of a landing: on some paths no finalize precedes it (sh EXIT trap with no landing done, ps1 console-window close, a finalize whose acknowledgement failed), and the close then lifts qa_approve's hold without an acknowledged landing — exactly what today's QA-claim supersede already does; under the legacy delivery policy the soft NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT warning is then the only guard, and strict policies still refuse. This is an explicit end-of-life call, not an idle signal. Do NOT close finalizing attempts in deleteWorker, the startup purge or any sweep — non-DEAD deletions are driven by lastActivityAt (rail); those gaps belong to task-686afecb5b844706be805f7cd86ba055. packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts, comment-only: closeHandedBackAttempts' doc (~483-487) must say a finalizing attempt ends only through moe.finalize_attempt or its runner's deregister_worker, no longer 'a later claim of the row supersedes it'. Error handling: a failed close never fails deregister_worker; it logs and leaves the attempt finalizing for the retry. Make step 2's case (4) and its variants green.

(3) docs/MCP_SERVER.md: the record_check_run (~117) and record_delivery_receipt (~119) premise lines and the 'Close on hand-back' paragraph (~121) — replace '(or the next claim of that row)' with '(or its runner's moe.deregister_worker)', say the next claim closes only running and reconciling leftovers, and that no other seat can own the row while its attempt is finalizing; moe.finalize_attempt (~457-488) and moe.record_candidate (~678) — replace 'when QA may already own the REVIEW task' with the rule (no other seat can claim the row until the attempt is finalized; the attempt fence is still the guard), note that a real finalize publishes a TASK_UPDATED, and add the escape (`outcome: 'failed'` by a governor or human for a runner that is gone); moe.claim_next_task 'Finalizing hold' (~1103) — keep the worker-scoped paragraph and add the task-scoped third-party rule: an explicit-taskId claim of a task whose attempt is finalizing under another worker is refused with retryable -32002 ATTEMPT_FINALIZING before any write, the ranked pool skips it, and an interactive (TUI) seat's row stays held until its operator closes the CLI and the wrapper finalizes; moe.wait_for_task (~1171) — the matcher skips the same rows and wakes when the boundary ends; moe.deregister_worker (~1647) — closes the worker's own finalizing attempts, including when its record was already pruned, a DEAD worker's retry is a quiet close-only no-op that still returns alreadyDead true, and a deregister without a finalize lifts qa_approve's hold without an acknowledged landing; moe.qa_approve finalizing hold (~1756) — a QA claim can no longer lift it, and it is lifted by finalize_attempt or the runner's deregister.

Phase 7+8 — Adversarial self-review, then complete. Answer in the task comment: (1) LIVENESS — every way a finalizing attempt now ends (finalize_attempt by its runner, its runner's deregister_worker even after the record was pruned, a governor or human finalize with outcome 'failed') and every shape that still holds a row: a wrapper killed with no exit trap (SIGKILL, power loss), deleteTask, set_task_status REVIEW→DONE (task-686afecb5b844706be805f7cd86ba055), and an interactive TUI seat, whose row stays held until its operator closes the CLI (codex runs the TUI for every role by default; a one-shot seat lands promptly). Confirm nothing new closes on an idle signal. (2) REJECT BYPASS — qa_reject has no finalizing hold and its ownership checks are no-ops on an unassigned row, so a human reject sends the row to WORKING with the attempt still finalizing; rework claims are then refused or skipped until the runner finalizes, and that worker's post-flight sees WORKING and lands a checkpoint, not a completion; cite case (7). (3) DEREGISTER WITHOUT FINALIZE — list the exit paths where it happens and state that qa_approve's hold then lifts without an acknowledged landing, as HEAD's supersede already does. (4) ORPHANS — task-2a7e0f5b's arm-3 cleanup of running and reconciling leftovers is untouched; cite the green cases. (5) LOCKSTEP — claim_next_task's ranked filter and wait_for_task's matcher use the same predicate; a QA waiter never wakes into a claim that returns nothing. (6) ORDERING AND CONCURRENCY — both refusals run before any write on the explicit path; claims, finalize_attempt and deregister_worker run serially under the state mutex; state which order yields which generation. (7) WRAPPER — through its post-flight the worker's attempt is the only open one, so moe_attempt_read passes and record_candidate is current; wrapper-side changes stay with task-49ec8755's rework. (8) DRIFT — tool descriptions outside the 10-file budget that now contradict the rule (recordCandidate.ts, claimGuards.ts, deregisterWorker.ts) are handed to task-686afecb5b844706be805f7cd86ba055. Then rerun `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` in packages/moe-daemon, call moe.declare_files for every path touched, and moe.complete_task with `verification: { command: 'npm test', exitCode: 0, outputTail }` and a summary naming the third-party refusal, the pool and wait skip, the finalize wake and the deregister close.

comments.author: worker-a7127038
comments.content:
WRAPPER HALF: what task-49ec8755's rework (worker-a7127038, 2026-09-14) builds, so this card does not duplicate it.
1. No qualityGate to run (unset, disabled, epic-deferred, or MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE): the landing records no candidate and reads no attempt identity. After a QA claim it lands exactly as it did before 49ec8755, with no rescue and no loop stop.
2. A gate that would run, while the pinned attempt is no longer current (closed or superseded by a claim, missing, reconciling, or unpinned): the wrapper does NOT run the gate. It records no CheckRun and does not bypass the evidence. It parks the frozen bytes on a rescue ref under MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE with an evidence-unavailable message, and posts no PUSH-BLOCKED gate announcement. The landing itself does not stop the worker loop.
3. finalize: the wrapper acknowledges only this seat's own finalizing attempt under the pinned identity. A closed, running, reconciling, missing or mismatched record is a no-op and the loop continues. A finalizing attempt with no pinned identity, or an exhausted acknowledgement, stops the loop. This is task-e47284ef's corrected ladder.
What stays for this card: making a gated completion that loses the QA-claim race still land with evidence. That needs the claim refusal, or a superseded finalizing attempt that record_candidate and finalize_attempt can still address. Case 2 above is the wrapper behaviour to expect until then.

comments.author: worker-a7127038
comments.content:
STEP 1: I confirmed the chain at HEAD d1b3d3a (branch moe/work-2026-09-13; 90277ac from task-2a7e0f5b is an ancestor). No code changed in this step.

(a) THE RACE
- completeTask.ts:149-152 puts the attempt in `finalizing` BEFORE the WORKING->REVIEW updateTask (:156-169) clears the seat.
- claimNextTask.ts:271-281: the worker-scoped hold only matches `a.workerId === params.workerId`, so qa-1 passes. The explicit path (:285-331) has no finalizing check. The assignment is written at :463, then openClaimAttempt runs at :487.
- In openClaimAttempt (:63-71), openAttempt throws ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN because finalizing is in OPEN_PHASES (attemptStore.ts:56-60). Arm 3 (:70) calls closeOpenAttempts, which closes the worker's finalizing attempt, and :71 opens QA's next generation.
- After that, qaApprove.ts:79 finds nothing to hold. The equality fence (enforcement.ts:148-193) refuses the worker's identity with ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED.

(b) WRAPPER AT HEAD
- moe_attempt_read (sh:1875-1893) and Read-MoeAttempt (ps1:1275-1288) require exactly one open attempt owned by this seat. After the supersede, the only open attempt is QA's, so the read fails with 'identity'. The result is MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, a rescue ref and a stopped loop.
- Both wrappers claim only through the ranked pool: sh:1641 CLAIM_JSON and ps1:558 $claimJson carry statuses and workerId, never a taskId. So the pool must skip silently rather than refuse.
- Live evidence consistent with this: refs/moe/rescue/task-49ec8755.../20260914T212120Z (a7042eb, Moe-Reason gate-failed, session worker-a7127038@2026-09-14T19:10:49Z). I did not re-prove its cause.
- Wrapper hardening stays with task-49ec8755's rework, which is still dirty and unlanded.

(c) NOTHING ELSE CLOSES IT
- These all select by assignment: releaseWorkerTasks (workerLifecycle.ts:127-128), deleteWorker (workerStore.ts:260-261), purgeAllWorkers (:415-416), and release_task's unassigned branch (releaseTask.ts:199-233).
- These skip finalizing: closeHandedBackAttempts (attemptStore.ts:468-472), reconcileRunningAttempts (:372), runReconcileWindowSweep (sweeps.ts:218). reattach refuses it (reattachAttempt.ts:177-190).
- The purge even SPARES a seat that holds a finalizing attempt (workersHoldingOpenAttempts, workerStore.ts:320-327).
- So a refusal with no close path would wedge the row, which is why the deregister close is needed.

(d) WAKE GAP
- attemptStore.ts:22-26 emits no event. wait_for_task reacts only to TASK_CREATED and TASK_UPDATED (waitForTask.ts:383).
- state.emit is @internal (StateManager.ts:978-979). It calls the emitter plus every subscriber, each in its own try/catch.
- Non-test subscribers:
  - waitForTask:356
  - waitForResource:143 (RESOURCE_UPDATED only)
  - chatWait:91 (MESSAGE_CREATED and CHANNEL_DELETED only)
- The emitter is wsServer.broadcast (index.ts:597-599), which re-serves TASK_UPDATED through deliveryProjection (WebSocketServer.ts:279-290).
- An extra TASK_UPDATED for an unchanged task therefore only re-runs the matcher and refreshes the board row.

(e) finalize_attempt has no ownership gate. OUTCOMES are landed|nothing-to-commit|rescued|failed (finalizeAttempt.ts:30), and an already-closed attempt replays at :200 before the fence runs. A governor or human can therefore close an abandoned boundary with outcome 'failed'.

(f) TESTS THAT DEPEND ON ARM 3 (five insert points in four tests)
- lifecycle.e2e.test.ts :150, :184, :205 (second completion is generation 3) and :234 (:246 is a direct updateTask with no attempt).
- governanceFeatures.test.ts:317.
- Staying green:
  - claimNextTask.test.ts:1239 and :1262 claim WORKING task-2 while the finalizing attempt sits on REVIEW task-1.
  - finalizeAttempt.test.ts:115-126 pins the persisted keys, and this change persists no new field.
  - delivery/acceptance.test.ts claims at :1052, :1109, :1152, :1324, :1766, :1882 and :1906, and none of them touches a row finalizing under another worker. In the candidate criterion (:1457-1560), QA only calls get_context before the finalize.

DESIGN DECISION: option A-refuse.
- Only the attempt's own worker may claim a task whose attempt is finalizing.
- An explicit-taskId claim from anyone else is refused with retryable -32002 ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, before any write.
- The ranked pool and the wait_for_task matcher skip the row through one shared predicate in util/claimEligibility.ts.
- A real finalize emits one TASK_UPDATED through a state-side helper.
- deregister_worker closes its own worker's finalizing attempts, keyed on attempt.workerId, so a pruned worker record is covered.
- Arm 3 still closes running and reconciling leftovers.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES
- Keeping the finalizing record acknowledgeable next to QA's attempt: this breaks assertNoOpenAttempt, currentAttempt, the equality fence, and both wrapper readers.
- A persisted supersede marker: needs a schema change.
- Wrapper-only option B: cannot restore qa_approve's hold, and the fence would still refuse the candidate a gated landing needs.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 10 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Option A-refuse (chosen): no seat other than the attempt's own worker may claim a task whose execution attempt is finalizing — explicit claims refuse with a retryable ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, the ranked pool and wait_for_task skip the row, a real finalize wakes waiters through one state-side helper, and deregister_worker closes its own worker's finalizing attempts (keyed on the attempt, so a pruned record is covered). It keeps every evidence property (record_candidate and finalize_attempt stay fenced to the current attempt), restores both holds, and makes the wrapper's exactly-one-open pre-check pass through the landing. Option A-keep-acknowledgeable (rejected): a finalizing attempt beside a new QA running attempt breaks assertNoOpenAttempt, currentAttempt and the equality fence in assertAttemptCurrent, and both wrappers' readers hard-fail on two open attempts. A persisted supersede marker (rejected): schema addition, and finalize_attempt persists no outcome. Option B wrapper-only (not this card): it cannot restore qa_approve's hold, and a gated landing still needs a candidate the fence refuses; its wrapper half belongs to task-49ec8755's rework. A refusal without a close path would wedge any row whose runner exits without finalizing, so the deregister close is part of this card; idle-free backstops for DEAD records, deleted tasks and REVIEW→DONE bypasses are split to task-686afecb5b844706be805f7cd86ba055.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: openClaimAttempt arm 3 is today the only automatic closer of a finalizing attempt: every release path selects tasks by assignment and complete_task unassigns the row. The worker-scoped finalizing hold refuses only the attempt's own worker; qa_approve's hold is task-scoped and runs before its ownership checks, but a QA claim defeats it first. attemptStore emits no events and state.emit is @internal to state/*, so the wake is a single state-side helper. The wrappers claim only through the ranked pool, so the explicit-path refusal is for directed claims. deregisterWorker's only production caller is tools/deregisterWorker.ts, reached only from wrapper exit and teardown paths. Four lifecycle tests (five insert points) depend on the supersede and must add the worker's finalize, as the real wrapper does.
planningNotes.risks: (1) Liveness: a wrapper killed with no exit trap leaves the row held until a governor finalizes it; interactive TUI seats hold their row until the operator closes the CLI. Both are documented; automated idle-free backstops are split to task-686afecb5b844706be805f7cd86ba055. (2) Reject bypass: a human qa_reject while finalizing sends the row to WORKING with the attempt still open; rework claims wait for the finalize and the worker lands a checkpoint instead of a completion. (3) Deregister without a finalize lifts qa_approve's hold without an acknowledged landing, as today's supersede already does; legacy policy warns only, strict policies refuse. (4) Test churn: five finalize inserts across four lifecycle tests; the rule is to add the finalize the real wrapper performs, never to weaken the refusal. (5) The refusal must stay limited to phase finalizing under a different worker, or task-2a7e0f5b's arm-3 orphan cleanup regresses. (6) File budget is at the 10-file cap; tool descriptions in recordCandidate.ts, claimGuards.ts and deregisterWorker.ts will read stale and are handed to the follow-up card.
